newsitem.title: USA: U.S. feedlot cattle trade active at $67 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. feedlot cattle trade active at $67 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. feedlot cattle sold at $67.00 per cwt in active trading, up $1.00 from Tuesday but unchanged from last week's top price, feedlot sources said.
About 11,000 head sold in Kansas, which brought the week to date estimate near 73,000, the sources said.
Sales in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area were pegged near 7,000 head, with a weekly movement estimated near 100,000, they said.
Fed cattle prices were lifted by active packer buying, which several feedlot sources tied to strong beef demand on Tuesday and Wednesday and outlooks for continued firm demand.

Beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.38 to up $0.31 per cwt, with 452 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported. Heavyweight choice was quoted down $0.13 at $99.25. Heavier-weight choice beef has declined $4.96 since March 25.
Recent price declines reportedly pushed beef values low enough to attracted renewed retail interest, sources said.

Fed cattle prices also were supported by expectations that a winter storm Thursday and Friday in Kansas could have a temporary impact on cattle shipments. Central and northern Kansas could get up to eight inches of snow and southern Kansas and the Oklahoma Panhandle could get freezing rain.
